# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 46

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 46:1 "so great and serious" vs. "so great and demanding"

- **EMET:** "since they are so great and serious"
- **LOGOS:** "given how great and demanding they are"
- **PNEUMA:** "They're so demanding and so serious"
- **Greek:** *tosoutan ousōn megalōn kai ischyrōn* — being so great and strong/demanding
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "given how great and demanding they are" (LOGOS). *Ischyros* = strong/powerful/demanding; "serious" (EMET) undersells the force.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 46:1 "has cleansed" vs. "have purified"

- **EMET:** "all who have cleansed their hearts"
- **LOGOS:** "all who have purified their hearts"
- **PNEUMA:** "everyone who has cleared their heart"
- **Greek:** *katharisantes tas kardias autōn* — having cleansed/purified their hearts
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "all who have purified their hearts" (LOGOS). "Purified" carries the cultic/ritual resonance of *katharizō* in religious contexts; "cleansed" is equally acceptable but SOPHIA follows the majority.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 46:2 "lives in death" vs. "shall die"

- **EMET:** "he shall live in death"
- **LOGOS:** "he shall die"
- **PNEUMA:** "that person is heading for death"
- **Greek:** *en thanatō zēsei* — he will live in death (paradox)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he shall live in death" (EMET). Hermas's phrase is deliberately paradoxical — to "live in death" means an existence that is death. LOGOS's simplification "shall die" loses the rhetorical force.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 46:2 "stumbles from time to time" vs. "stumbles at times"

- **EMET:** "stumbles from time to time"
- **LOGOS:** "even if he stumbles at times"
- **PNEUMA:** "even though they stumble sometimes"
- **Greek:** *ean de kai ptaisē pote* — if also he stumbles at some point
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "even if he stumbles at times" (LOGOS). The conditional "even if" preserves the gracious concession Hermas makes.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 46:3 "wanderings" vs. "transgressions"

- **EMET:** "forgives him all his wanderings"
- **LOGOS:** "forgives him all his transgressions"
- **PNEUMA:** "forgiving all their stumbling and wandering"
- **Greek:** *aphiēsin autō pasas tas hamartias* — forgives him all his sins/transgressions
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "forgives him all his transgressions" (LOGOS). *Hamartia* = sin/transgression; EMET's "wanderings" is too soft for this term.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 46:4 "lives in forgetfulness" vs. "lives carelessly"

- **EMET:** "the man who lives in forgetfulness"
- **LOGOS:** "the man who lives in forgetfulness"
- **PNEUMA:** "someone who lives carelessly, forgetting God"
- **Greek:** *en lēthē zōnta* — living in forgetfulness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the man who lives in forgetfulness" (EMET/LOGOS). *Lēthē* is a rich term — the river of forgetfulness, oblivion. "Carelessly" (PNEUMA) loses this theological dimension.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 46:4 "torments" vs. "afflicts" vs. "chastises"

- **EMET:** "this angel torments that man for his wickedness, and he is chastised"
- **LOGOS:** "that angel afflicts him for his wickedness and he is chastised"
- **PNEUMA:** "who torments them for their wickedness. That torment is corrective"
- **Greek:** *basanizei auton...paideuetai* — torments/afflicts him...he is disciplined/trained
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "that angel chastises him for his wickedness unto salvation." The verb *basanizō* does mean "torment/afflict"; SOPHIA collapses the two verbs to preserve the corrective-toward-salvation point concisely.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 46:5 "love of humanity" vs. "philanthropy"

- **EMET:** "love of humanity"
- **LOGOS:** "philanthropy"
- **PNEUMA:** "love for humanity"
- **Greek:** *philanthrōpia* — love of mankind, philanthropy
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "philanthropy" (LOGOS). As a Greek theological term with a technical history in Christian writing, it is worth retaining as a transliteration-loan rather than translating.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 46:5 "long-suffering" vs. "forbearance" vs. "patience"

- **EMET:** "long-suffering"
- **LOGOS:** "forbearance"
- **PNEUMA:** "patience"
- **Greek:** *makrothymia* — long-suffering, patient endurance, forbearance
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "forbearance" (LOGOS). All three translations are acceptable; "forbearance" captures the restrained endurance sense of *makrothymia* most precisely.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 46:5 "so long as a man repents, he has hope"

- **EMET:** "as long as a man repents he has hope"
- **LOGOS:** "so long as a man repents, he has hope of salvation"
- **PNEUMA:** "as long as someone is capable of repenting, there is hope"
- **Greek:** *hōs an metanoē anthrōpos, elpida echei* — as long as a man repents, he has hope
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "so long as a man repents, he has hope" (EMET). LOGOS adds "of salvation" — accurate in context but beyond the Greek. PNEUMA changes "repents" to "is capable of repenting" — a significant theological shift.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 46.*
